item.title: Cross-Linked Halide Networks for Lithium Superionic Conduction

Journal of the American Chemical Society | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in a polyanion-assisted cross-linking strategy that suppresses nonbridging oxygens and promotes bridging-oxygen coordination in Cl/O halide networks, creating a frustrated energy landscape for fast Li+ conduction. Significance: ZrCl4-xLi3PO4 achieves 2.8×10–3 S cm–1 at 30 °C, humidity tolerance, and stable cycling at 55 °C and 4.6 V, establishing cross-linking topochemistry as a design principle for robust halide electrolytes.
🏷 solid electrolyte · halide superionic conductor · polyanion cross-linking · nonbridging oxygen · all-solid-state battery

Journal of the American Chemical Society | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in a Na+-based NZSP coating that dynamically undergoes Li+/Na+ exchange during cycling, forming a fast Li+ conductor while incorporating Na+ into the NCM811 lattice as pillar support. This couples interfacial protection with bulk lattice reinforcement, suppressing parasitic reactions and chemo-mechanical degradation. It enables 4.7 V stability and a 557 Wh kg–1 pouch cell, advancing high-energy Ni-rich lithium batteries.

💡 The novelty lies in identifying interfacial acid–base kinetics, not CO poisoning, as the concentration-limiting factor in DFAFCs, and using cation-pinning via Dy2O3-modified Rh single atoms to stabilize OH–, invert local pH, and enrich formate. 💡 The novelty lies in using electrophoretic deposition with HEC and PAA binders to strengthen cathode coatings on carbon fibres, addressing cracking and debonding in structural battery positive electrodes. Significance: binders more than double shear strength, and binder chemistry critically governs the trade-off between mechanical strength, electronic connectivity, and ionic transport, offering a design strategy for multifunctional structural battery electrodes.

Advanced Energy Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in a ternary hybrid electrolyte combining Zn(OTf)₂/LiOTf dual salts with 5 vol.% EMIMTFSI ionic liquid, where ion pairs rebuild the hydrogen-bond network to lower viscosity and widen the electrochemical window to 2.76 V. Advanced Energy Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in using diethyl phosphoramidate as an ion-pair decoupler that reshapes Li+ solvation chemistry in polymer electrolytes, boosting room-temperature conductivity 24.6-fold. Significance: this single-molecule design simultaneously enables fast ionic conduction, stable cycling (850 h; 96.5% retention after 400 cycles), and intrinsic flame retardancy, establishing solvation-chemistry tuning as a new paradigm for safe room-temperature solid polymer electrolytes.

Advanced Energy Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in using amorphous SiO₂ as an additive in Na metal anodes via accumulative roll bonding, forming an in situ inorganic-rich SEI (SiOₓ/Na₂O/NaF) that enhances ion transport and mechanical robustness. Its significance is enabling dendrite suppression, ultralow overpotential (24 mV), 1350 h cycling, and 8000-cycle stability, offering a scalable route to durable sodium metal batteries.
